source: Seven learner attempts saved as one batch, including the immediate final retry
lessonTheme: Negative command objects, publicar spelling and gender repair
summary: Initial negative creesla corrected to No la crees, then correctly used no la revises, affirmative revísala and masculine no lo revises. Introduced publica/no publiques c → qu spelling; no lo publiques correct. Affirmative publícala was grammatical for feminine but mismatched logo target; immediately retried publícalo with es un logo explanation. Written command accents supplied.

observations.outcome: After negative-object placement model No la revises, learner attached la to negative crees. Corrected to no + la + crees; negative verb form and object gender were already right.
Correct negative object placement after correction, with feminine la for función.
Correct switch to affirmative command with attached la; accent/capitalization supplied.
Correct transfer to masculine lo for stated el logo. Tutor then introduced publica / no publiques and c → qu to preserve sound before e.
Correct no lo publiques after bare no publiques model: object placed before verb and qu spelling retained.

Grammatical affirmative command for a feminine object after accent supplied. Prompt still referred to el logo, so meaning did not match masculine target. Tutor acknowledged feminine form and supplied Publícalo; no command-formation error beyond accent.

Correct immediate retry with masculine lo and explicit grammatical explanation es un logo. Accent/capitalization supplied. Actual publishing was neither requested nor performed; these are lesson examples.

nextSteps: Combine negative publicar with a familiar reason clause and explicit feminine referent

assessmentNote: Grammatical different-meaning answers are distinct from exact target matches. Immediate correction/retry does not establish delayed mastery. No repository publication was performed in response to classroom commands.
